```{r policy-models, include=FALSE}
# linear_models.R only DEFINES when sourced; the models are fitted here, on
# every knit, from whatever is currently in the export. Roughly four seconds for
# the six, so there is nothing to cache.
lm_data   <- policy_model_data(pilot)
lm_models <- fit_policy_models(lm_data)
```

```{r lm-definitions, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# The outcome definitions are written out from the constant itself rather than
# retyped into the prose, so the box cannot describe a grouping the models do
# not use.
cat('<div class="block-box">\n<strong>The outcomes.</strong> Each is the mean of',
    'the <em>beleid</em> sliders for the substances named, so it stays on the',
    'sliders\' own scale: 0 = <em>verbod</em>, 100 = <em>vrije verkoop</em>.',
    'The last two are unions of the first three.\n<ul>\n')
for (name in names(POLICY_OUTCOME_SETS))
  cat("<li><code>", name, "</code> &mdash; ",
      paste(POLICY_OUTCOME_SETS[[name]], collapse = ", "), "</li>\n", sep = "")
cat('</ul>\n')

cat('<strong>Pijnstillers appear in no outcome.</strong> They are legal on',
    'prescription, and the item cannot separate prescribed use from the rest,',
    'so <code>beleid_pijnstillers</code> is left out of all five &mdash; as in',
    'the substance splits in the descriptives tab, which exclude them from both',
    'the legal and the illicit set. The main study asks own use per substance',
    '<em>group</em> (alcohol, tabak, softdrugs, harddrugs), so there is no',
    'painkiller use item to enter as a predictor.\n<br><br>\n')

cat('<strong>Note that <code>softdrugs</code> here is not the grouping the',
    'descriptives tab uses.</strong> The substance ladder counts psychedelica',
    'as a hard drug; here it is grouped with cannabis. The two answer different',
    'questions &mdash; the ladder is about what a respondent has used, these',
    'sets about which policies are averaged together &mdash; and they are not',
    'interchangeable.\n<br><br>\n')

cat('<strong>The candidate predictors</strong> are the', length(lm_data$predictors),
    'items of the belief, behaviour, own-use and emotion blocks. Beliefs and',
    'behaviour enter as their reverse-scored copies, so that high means',
    '"more pro-liberalisation" on every item; without that a coefficient\'s sign',
    'would record how an item happened to be worded. The',
    '<em>geen van deze</em> emotion boxes are excluded: each is 1 exactly when',
    'its topic\'s other three are 0.\n<br><br>\n')

cat('<strong>Selection</strong> is stepwise on AIC in both directions',
    '(<code>step(..., direction = "both")</code>): it starts from the full set',
    'and may at each step drop a term or take back one it dropped earlier.\n<br><br>\n')

cat('<strong>The five item models are fitted on the same',
    nrow(lm_data$frame), 'respondents</strong>, of', nrow(pilot),
    'in the sample &mdash; the complete cases over every outcome and every',
    'candidate predictor. That is required rather than tidy:',
    '<code>step()</code> needs the model frame to stay fixed as terms enter and',
    'leave, and it is also what makes the five comparable to each other.\n<br><br>\n')

cat('<strong>The last model is the baseline the other five are read against.</strong>',
    'It predicts the broadest outcome from the demographic questions alone.',
    'Each question enters with all of its answer options: the panel agency\'s',
    'recodes of age, sex, education, urbanisation and vote recall.\n<br><br>\n')

cat('<strong>How the terms read.</strong> <em>leeftijd</em> is stored as an',
    '<em>ordered</em> factor of the seven QSF age bands, which R fits with',
    'polynomial contrasts, so the table carries <code>leeftijd.L</code>,',
    '<code>leeftijd.Q</code> and so on &mdash; trends across the bands. The',
    'other four enter as unordered factors, one term per answer against the',
    'first, labelled with the value labels of the agency\'s .sav.\n<br><br>\n')

if (nrow(lm_data$demographic_frame) != nrow(lm_data$frame))
  cat('<strong>It has its own', nrow(lm_data$demographic_frame),
      'respondents</strong>, not the', nrow(lm_data$frame),
      'the other five use, because the two frames take the complete cases over',
      'different columns. One shared',
      'frame would have taken those respondents out of all six models to serve',
      'this one. Read its <em>R</em>&sup2; against the others with that in',
      'mind: it is a different sample, not only a different set of',
      'predictors.\n<br><br>\n')

cat('<strong>Reading a table.</strong> One row per predictor stepwise selection',
    'kept, sorted by |<em>t</em>| rather than by the order the terms sit in the',
    'formula, with the statement each one stands for in full. Beliefs and',
    'behaviour are reverse-scored, so a positive <em>b</em> always means',
    '&ldquo;more agreement with the pro-liberalisation reading of this item goes',
    'with a higher policy score&rdquo;. The printed <code>summary()</code> is',
    'still there, folded under each table.\n<br><br>\n')

cat('<strong>How much weight these can carry.</strong>',
    length(lm_data$predictors), 'candidate predictors on', nrow(lm_data$frame),
    'observations. At that ratio stepwise selection returns an optimistic',
    '<em>R</em>&sup2; and a term set that is unstable to resampling, and the',
    '<em>p</em>-values below are computed as if the model had been specified in',
    'advance rather than chosen from the data.\n</div>\n')
```

```{r lm-model-helper, echo=TRUE}
# One table per model: every retained
# predictor sorted by |t|, the statement it stands for in full, and the printed
# summary one click away rather than as the presentation.
#
# The two sets of models ask the same question of different samples, so the
# layouts are the same on purpose - a difference in layout would read as a
# difference in method. model_coefficients() is in R/linear_models.R; this
# function only prints what it returns.
model_table <- function(fit, label, id, candidates, note) {
  s   <- summary(fit)
  tab <- model_coefficients(fit)
  cat("\n\n<h2 id='lm-model-", id, "'>", label, "</h2>\n", sep = "")
  cat("<p style='color:#555;font-size:0.9em'>R&sup2; = ",
      sprintf("%.3f", s$r.squared), " &middot; aangepaste R&sup2; = ",
      sprintf("%.3f", s$adj.r.squared), " &middot; alle ", nrow(tab),
      " behouden voorspellers van de ", candidates,
      " kandidaten &middot; n = ", stats::nobs(fit), " &middot; ", note,
      "</p>\n", sep = "")
  print(knitr::kable(tab, row.names = FALSE, format = "html",
                     table.attr = 'class="table table-sm"'))
  cat("\n\n<details><summary>Volledige samenvatting</summary>\n\n```\n")
  print(s)
  cat("\n```\n\n</details>\n")
}
```

```{r lm-models, echo=TRUE, results='asis'}
# The five item models and the demographic baseline differ in three things -
# their label, their candidate pool and their note - so they are one loop with
# those three resolved per model rather than two loops that could drift.
for (name in names(lm_models)) {
  demographic <- !name %in% names(POLICY_OUTCOME_SETS)
  model_table(
    fit   = lm_models[[name]],
    label = if (demographic)
              paste(name, "&mdash; dezelfde uitkomst, voorspeld uit wie de",
                    "respondent is")
            else
              paste0(name, " &mdash; gemiddelde beleidsslider over ",
                     paste(POLICY_OUTCOME_SETS[[name]], collapse = ", ")),
    id    = gsub("(^-|-$)", "", gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "-", tolower(name))),
    candidates = if (demographic) length(lm_data$demographics)
                 else length(lm_data$predictors),
    note  = if (demographic) "voorspellers: de vijf demografische vragen"
            else "voorspellers uit het belief-, gedrags-, gebruiks- en emotieblok")
}
```
